title: Phase 3 Study of Romiplostim Plus Predniso(lo)ne vs. Predniso(lo)ne Alone for the Treatment of Previously Untreated Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
official:
A Phase 3, Randomized, Multicenter, Open-label Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Romiplostim Plus Predniso(lo)ne vs. Predniso(lo)ne Alone for the Treatment of
Adults With Previously Untreated Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
summary: Main objective: To compare durable platelet response in participants randomized to romiplostim with predniso(lo)ne versus predniso(lo)ne alone
conditions: Diagnosis of primary ITP according to the 2019 International Consensus Report that is previously untreated and requires treatment

interventions.name: Nplate 500 micrograms powder for solution for injection

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed informed consent includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.
2. Age ≥ 18 years or ≥ legal age within the country if it is older than 18 years at the time of signing the informed consent.
3. Diagnosis of primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) according to the 2019 International Consensus Report (ICR) that is previously untreated and requires treatment.
4. Any platelet count less than 30 × 109/L before any medical intervention in an individual or platelet count less than 50 × 109/L with concomitant clinically significant bleeding symptoms before any medical intervention.
5. Participants must use protocol-specified contraception, during treatment and for an additional period of one month after the last dose of IMP(s).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of life-threatening bleeding unless the participant is medically stable and has returned to clinical baseline before randomization.
2. Participant with active systemic infection or symptoms that indicate an acute and/or uncontrolled infection within 7 days before the first dose of trial treatment, unless course of antimicrobial therapy has been completed by first dose of trial treatment. Note: Simple urinary tract infections and uncomplicated bacterial pharyngitis are permitted if responding to active treatment.
3. Venous thrombotic event within 3 months before randomization or arterial thrombotic event (eg, transient ischemic attack or stroke) within 6 months before randomization.
4. Major surgery within 28 days or minor surgery within 3 days before randomization.
5. Symptomatic ischemia or uncontrolled arrhythmia, and/or moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA Functional Classification III, IV) at baseline.
6. Uncontrolled hypertension before randomization.
7. Inadequately treated cardiovascular conditions including cardiomyopathy, major congenital heart disease, or second- or third-degree atrioventricular block within 4 months before randomization
8. Abnormal hepatic or renal function at screening as determined by any of the following:  • total bilirubin > 1.5 x ULN  • alanine aminotransferase [ALT] or aspartate aminotransferase [AST] > 3 x ULN  • creatinine clearance < 45 mL/min as calculated using Cockcroft Gault formula
9. Receipt of live and live-attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks before randomization, or planned to receive during the time of the proposed study. Administration of inactivated (killed) vaccines is acceptable.
10. History of total splenectomy.
11. Prior ITP-directed therapy; however, emergency ITP therapy is allowed before the first dose of study drug without wash-out period but limited to the following maximum doses and durations:  •Predniso(lo)ne: 1 mg/kg/day for 3 consecutive days  • Dexamethasone: 40 mg/day for 1 day or a total of 40 mg over 2 consecutive days  • Methylprednisolone: 1 mg/kg/day for 1 day or total of 1 mg/kg/day over 2 consecutive days  • IVIg: 2 g/kg over 2 consecutive days  • Anti-D: 50 µg/kg as a single dose for 1 day  • Platelet transfusion: as needed for up to 3 days
12. Participant has known sensitivity or intolerance to any of the products to be administered during study (eg, uncontrolled diabetes) or to any Escherichia coli-derived product (eg, filgrastim, pegfilgrastim, certain insulins).
13. Received rituximab (for any indication) before randomization
14. Alkylating agents within 8 weeks before randomization.
15. Use of concurrent anticoagulation therapy and/or antiplatelet therapy.
16. Need for nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) use and use of NSAIDs within 7 days before randomization
17. Currently receiving a trial intervention, or less than 30 days or 5 half-lives if known (whichever is later) since ending a trial intervention in another investigational device or drug trial.
18. Participant unlikely to be able to complete all protocol-required visits or procedures, restrictions and requirements, in the judgment of the individual and investigator.
19. History or evidence of any other clinically significant disorder, condition, or disease that, in the opinion of the investigator, would pose a risk to participant safety.
20. Currently pregnant (confirmed with positive pregnancy test) or breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant, donate eggs, or breastfeed while on trial until an additional period of one month after the last dose of IMP(s).
21. Other cytopenias except for iron-deficient anemia.
22. Known autoimmune diseases other than ITP.
23. Known drug-induced thrombocytopenia.
24. Known human immunodeficiency virus infection.
25. Known active chronic hepatitis of any cause.
26. Active or prior malignancy except for malignancy treated with curative intent and with no known active disease present for ≥ 3 years before randomization (no time period needed for basal cell carcinoma) and felt to be at low risk for recurrence by the treating physician.
27. Other hematopoietic disorders (leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, etc.) or known history of a bone marrow stem cell disorder.
